title: Feed Pumps in Steam Systems - Suction Lift Head vs. Temperature
description: Cavitation of impellers increases with water temperatures. This tool helps determine safe suction lift and pressure head limits based on feeding water temperature to avoid cavitation in feed pumps.

title.text: Suction Lift Head vs Water Temperature

components.content: Chart showing the relationship between water temperature and suction/pressure head limits

## Important Information

**Cavitation Risk:** Cavitation of impellers increases with water temperatures.

**Temperature Threshold:** For water with temperature above **80°C (175°F)**, it is necessary to use a positive pressure head with the pump located at an elevation below the water or condensate receiver.

**Common Operating Conditions:** In steam distribution systems, open vented condensate receivers typically operate with temperatures close to **100°C (212°F)**, especially in systems where:
- Most of the steam consumed is returned as hot condensate
- Make-up water is heated to reduce dissolved air content
